questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Russia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Russia article.

questions.proof: Moscow, Russia's capital city, is the largest city entirely in Europe by population; it is also Europe's largest city by area.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Russia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Russia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Russia article.

questions.proof: The most southern point is in Caucasus, on the border with Azerbaijan.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Russia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Russia article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “By total area (17,098,242 square kilometers or 6,601,668 square miles), it is the largest country in the world, followed by _____, and the United States or China.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “followed”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Russia article.

questions.proof: By total area (17,098,242 square kilometers or 6,601,668 square miles), it is the largest country in the world, followed by Canada, and the United States or China.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This includes Crimea, LPR, DPR, Kherson Oblast and Zaporizhzhia Oblast and Sevastopol, which are claimed by both Russia and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Russia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Russia article.

questions.proof: This includes Crimea, LPR, DPR, Kherson Oblast and Zaporizhzhia Oblast and Sevastopol, which are claimed by both Russia and Ukraine.
